description: Given an integer array nums, return true if there exists a triple of indices (i, j, k) such that i < j < k and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k]. The algorithm should run in O(n) time and O(1) space.
intuition: Track two thresholds: the smallest value seen and the smallest value greater than it. If you find anything larger than both, you have your increasing triplet. Even if the first threshold updates later, the second still has a valid predecessor somewhere before it.
approach: Track two variables: first (smallest seen) and second (smallest number greater than first). If we find a number greater than second, we have an increasing triplet.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: nums = [5,1,4,2,3]
firstMin=Inf, secondMin=Inf

num=5: 5<=Inf → firstMin=5
num=1: 1<=5 → firstMin=1
num=4: 4>1, 4<=Inf → secondMin=4
  (1 < 4 exists earlier in the array)
num=2: 2>1, 2<=4 → secondMin=2
  (1 < 2 still has a valid predecessor)
num=3: 3>firstMin=1, 3>secondMin=2 → return true!
  Triplet: 1 < 2 < 3
explanation:
1. first = smallest value seen so far.
2. second = smallest value greater than some previous first.
3. If we find n > second, there must be a first < second < n triplet.
4. Even if first gets updated after second, the old first still exists before second.
hints: Track the two smallest values in increasing order.
If you find a value greater than both, you have a triplet.
Updating first does not invalidate second: second still has a smaller predecessor.
